'''Ronald Walsworth''' is an American physicist, engineer, and professor at the [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://walsworth.umd.edu/people/ron-walsworth/|title=Ron Walsworth &#124; Walsworth Group|website=walsworth.umd.edu}}</ref>

== Career ==
Walsworth earned a B.S. in physics from [[Duke University]] in 1984 and completed a  Ph.D. in physics from [[Harvard University|Harvard]] in 1991.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://sites.duke.edu/qdsworkshop/speakers/ronald-walsworth/ | title=Ronald Walsworth – Quantum Devices & Systems Manufacturing Workshop }}</ref> He has been recognized for his contributions to science. In 2001, he was elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2001&unit_id=GPMFC&institution= | title=Honors and Award Winners }}</ref> He was a Distinguished Traveling Lecturer for the American Physical Society from 2002 to 2023. In 2005, he received the [[Francis M. Pipkin Award]] in Precision Measurements from the American Physical Society.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prize Recipient |url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm |access-date=2023-09-14 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref> He also received the Smithsonian Institution Exceptional Service Award; the Duke University Faculty Scholar Award; and the [[NASA Group Achievement Award]].

Since 2020, Walsworth has served as the Founding Director of the Quantum Technology Center at the University of Maryland;<ref>{{Cite web |title=Quantum Technology Center |url=https://qtc.umd.edu/ |access-date=2023-09-14 |website=qtc.umd.edu}}</ref> and also as a Minta Martin Professor in the Department of Physics<ref>{{Cite web |last=Suplee |first=Anne |title=Walsworth, Ronald - UMD Physics |url=https://umdphysics.umd.edu/people/faculty/current/item/1194-rwalswor.html |access-date=2023-09-14 |website=umdphysics.umd.edu |language=en-us}}</ref> and in the Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering<ref>{{Cite web |title=Walsworth, Ronald {{!}} Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering |url=https://ece.umd.edu/clark/faculty/1205/Ronald-Walsworth |access-date=2023-09-14 |website=ece.umd.edu}}</ref> at the University of Maryland. He previously served as a Senior Physicist at the Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory and as a Senior Lecturer in the Department of Physics at Harvard University.

Walsworth has helped establish several startup companies.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ronald Walsworth LinkedIn |url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/ronald-walsworth-19014733/}}</ref> In 2012, he co-founded [[Quantum Diamond Technologies]] with [[Mikhail Lukin]] and others to develop biomedical diagnostic technology using [[Nitrogen-vacancy center|nitrogen-vacancy]] diamond magnetic imaging.<ref>https://qdti.com/</ref> In 2014, he co-founded Hyperfine with [[Matthew S. Rosen|Matthew Rosen]] and [[Jonathan Rothberg]] to develop the world's first portable human [[Magnetic resonance imaging|MRI]] instrument able to move to a patient's bedside at the point of care.<ref>https://hyperfine.io/</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.science.org/content/article/mri-all-cheap-portable-scanners-aim-revolutionize-medical-imaging | title=MRI for all: Cheap portable scanners aim to revolutionize medical imaging }}</ref> In 2020, he founded [[Quantum Catalyzer]] to perform quantum research and create new quantum technology startups;<ref>https://www.q-cat.io/</ref> one of these companies is QDM.IO, co-founded by Walsworth and geologist [[Roger Fu]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Roger Fu |url=https://eps.harvard.edu/people/roger-fu |access-date=2023-09-14 |website=eps.harvard.edu |language=en}}</ref> which builds and sells [[Quantum diamond microscope|quantum diamond microscopes]] (QDMs) for research and education.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Home |url=https://www.qdm.io/ |access-date=2023-09-14 |website=QDM Site |language=en}}</ref>

In 2024, Walsworth joined [[Quantum Coast Capital]] as an advisor, leveraging his extensive expertise in quantum science and technology to guide the [[venture capital]] firm in identifying and nurturing innovative startups in the quantum ecosystem. His role involves shaping strategies for investment in quantum technologies and fostering collaborations between research institutions and industry to accelerate advancements in the field.
